newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African industrial shares braved an early buffetting at the hands of the futures market on Friday to power ahead and end the day firmly up on positive underlying sentiment, dealers said.
The futures near-dated contracts close-out at noon (1000 GMT) saw a volatile morning of spikes and troughs with futures dealers driving prices both up and down as they rushed to settle positions.
But the bulls won out in the end and the afternoon saw the market build on the gains as the rand and local bond market gave a boost to the market's mood.
"We ended up after the close-out and the really encouraging thing was that we continued to rise after that," one dealer said.
The all-share index added 25.0 points to 7,234.1 as industrials put on 77.7 points to end at 8,511.5.
Volumes were a healthy 1.3 billion rand worth of trade, though most of it was futures-related.

Dealers and portfolio managers said the market was set to continue its positive tone into next week as a raft of economic data -- including the May Consumer Price Index figure, M3 money supply, private credit and trade balance -- is seen giving shares an upwards lift.

"At the end of the next few weeks, I think you will be able to look back and see the index higher than it was at the start of the week," said Malcolm Chapman, general manager at Absa Asset Management.

The futures close-out had earlier spooked dealers with the prospect of knocking industrials in a manipulated market, but though it was busy in volume terms it was less topsy-turvy than most close-outs.
The all-share June contract was last at 6,480/97 from 6,475 settlement as industrials were at 8,025/45 from 8,004 settlement.
The gold contract was asked at 745 from a settlement of 746.

The close-out and a huge two billion rand overseas deal from broker SBC Warburg on Wednesday saw weekly volumes hit a new record of 5.844 billion rands worth of trade, beating the previous best of 4.750 billion rands in the week to end April 25.
However, the gold index had another disastrous day as bullion price woes continued to wreak havoc in the sector, with dealers saying there was little prospect of recovery on the horizon.
Bullion fixed in London at $338.00 an ounce -- a four month low -- late on Friday.
The local index fell 33.9 points, or 3.19 percent, to hit a new lowest level since March, 1993, of 1,027.4. Vaal Reefs dropped 475 cents to 238.75 rand and Kloof fell 75 cents to 27.00 rand.
Among other individual shares the overall market showed 211 stocks advancing, against 168 dropping. New highs were hit by 25 shares while 36 counters sank to new lows.
Warburg was again active in heavily traded stocks by doing deals in Johnnic and CG Smith.
Johnnic saw a 1.24 million share foreign trade as it rose 50 cents to 58.00 rand and CG Smith foreign deal of 449,000 shares and added 20 cents to 23.75 rand.
Information technology firm Persetel jumped nine rand to 36.00 rand on speculation that the firm may announce a deal soon, possibly involving rival Q Data which ended up four cents to 852 cents.
-- Paul Harris, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
